Lemma
[Circle-pattern convexity] 1. 13.7.3\group circle-patterns Source: thurston:page-0358, thurston:page-0359, thurston:page-0360

The angle equations for the circle pattern are the gradient equations of a strictly convex functional in logarithmic radii, modulo the Euclidean scaling direction. Consequently a solution is unique, and the variational argument proves existence whenever the combinatorial angle inequalities hold.
Proof

\sketch Differentiate the three-circle cosine-law relation around each face. The Hessian is a sum of positive semidefinite face contributions whose only common kernel is constant scaling; the boundary behavior of the functional is controlled by the circuit inequalities.

□
